note: Direct-REST-equivalent checks for v1.2's contract.md §6.H / §8 'calls that must fail' rows and AC-21.4/AC-21.8, run against the live Supabase project (dufyzxtrhdcwrebagsfs). Same methodology as ac-5.2-11.1-11.2-sql-verification.json.
methodology_deviation: This sandbox's egress proxy returns 403 for dufyzxtrhdcwrebagsfs.supabase.co on every raw HTTPS attempt (confirmed again this pass: `curl` to the REST endpoint gets `CONNECT tunnel failed, response 403`), so a literal HTTP PATCH via curl or a real Chromium fetch() is not possible from this sandbox (same limitation as the v1.1 pass). The Supabase MCP connector (mcp__Supabase__execute_sql) is reachable (does not go through this sandbox's local egress proxy). Each check below runs as `set role anon; <statement>;` inside a Supabase SQL session, which exercises the exact same column grants, RLS policies and CHECK constraint (contract.md §1-§3) that PostgREST enforces for the anon/publishable-key role on a real REST call — not a literal HTTP request. Flagged as a deviation per contract.md's own guidance; a literal HTTP-level re-run against LIVE_URL's Supabase project is recommended once real network access is available (e.g. Dathan's phone or a CI runner with real egress), but is not expected to behave differently since the enforcement point (Postgres grants + RLS + CHECK constraint) is identical either way.
